title: Explicit compatible resolution presentations for finite-cover derived sections
statement:
Use the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. A finite-cover derived-section presentation consists of the following explicit data, with no existence or invertibility assertion. Let $J=I^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a small filtered category and $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a strict diagram of small categories with finite limits and finite covering precoverages stable under finite composition and base change [def-weil-pbc-finite-precoverage]. The transition functors preserve finite limits and coverings. Give a colimit cocone $V$ and its finite-cover colimit site as in [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites], with its actual projection functors. Write $A_i=\operatorname{Ab}(F(i))$ and $A=\operatorname{Ab}(V)$.
A complex system consists of cochain complexes $K_i$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and adjoint transitions $K_i\to f_{a*}K_j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws. Its coefficient colimit is a diagram of the actual inverse-image complexes with transitions specified by the adjunction units and those transitions, together with a colimit cocone $C$ and its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
For an integer $b$, a resolution model consists of a compatible degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism $K_i\to J_i$ with all $J_i^n$ injective and $J_i^n=0$ for $n<b$, their K-injectivity in the sense of [def-sp-kinjective-bridge], a similarly bounded-below injective resolution $C\to R$ on the colimit site, and compatible adjoint maps $J_i\to p_{i*}R$ extending the actual coprojections after the augmentations. Include the diagram $B_i=\Gamma(F(i),J_i)$ and a cocone into $\Gamma(V,R)$, with every transition and leg specified by the section map of the corresponding adjoint map. Global sections are evaluation at terminal objects. The chain comparison is the canonical colimit-desc map $\operatorname{colim}_i B_i\to\Gamma(V,R)$.
A compatible change of sites consists of an index functor, finite-limit and cover preserving functors at stages and at the limit, coherent square isomorphisms and coherent projection isomorphisms. A coefficient change consists of adjoint coefficient maps satisfying these squares and the induced colimit map specified on actual coprojections. A lifted change consists of compatible maps of stage resolutions and receiving resolutions extending the coefficient maps, with their normalized section maps. Ordinary coefficient maps, resolution refinements, and canonical upper truncation towers [def-kun-truncations] are given the same explicit equations. The derived continuity square means equality of the two composites after localization in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$; no such equality is included as an assumption in the definition of a lifted change.
